title: Erlotinib monotherapy
scope_note: NCCP 00219a is first-line EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC; 00219b is switch-maintenance after stable disease following first-line chemotherapy; 00219c is after failure of at least one previous chemotherapy regimen. Global NCCP eligibility requires a validated activating EGFR mutation in each setting. These are advanced-disease settings, not adjuvant treatment.

purpose: Erlotinib blocks abnormal EGFR growth signals in selected lung cancers. Treatment aims to control advanced cancer and delay progression.

agents.name: Erlotinib
agents.explanation: Erlotinib blocks the EGFR tyrosine kinase signal that can drive growth in cancers with activating EGFR mutations. Effects on normal skin and bowel cells also contribute to side effects.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea, rash, breathing changes and eye symptoms promptly.
risks: Rare bowel perforation and serious skin reactions

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: The usual dose is 150 mg by mouth once daily, continuously without a planned rest week. Use the dose on your prescription. Treatment continues while it helps and side effects remain acceptable; any change is agreed with your team.

sections.title: Before starting
sections.text: Confirm the mutation, treatment setting, prescription, baseline tests, first review and emergency contact.

sections.title: Taking the tablets
sections.text: Take at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food. If a dose is missed, do not replace it; take the usual next dose. If you vomit within a few hours after taking it, do not repeat the dose. Ask pharmacy before changing smoking habits or adding medicines for stomach acid.

sections.title: Supplies and visits
sections.text: Arrange the next prescription before tablets run out. Keep your blood-test and clinic appointments. The oral regimen itself does not require an infusion line or pump.

sections.title: If treatment is held
sections.text: Ask why, what must recover and when review is due. Only the team authorises restarting or changing dose.

sections.title: At treatment change
sections.text: Agree ongoing symptom care, scans, contraception and follow-up.

evidence.title: Evidence for this treatment setting
evidence.intro: The mutation and prior treatment matter.
evidence.interpretation: In a study of previously untreated EGFR-mutated advanced lung cancer, erlotinib delayed progression compared with chemotherapy. The final survival comparison did not show a statistically significant difference. The study population and subsequent treatments matter; ask how the evidence applies to your exact setting.
evidence.limitations: Study groups cannot predict your individual outcome or compare treatments from different trials.

teachback: Explain when you take the daily tablet and how food affects it.
What will you do after a missed dose?
Which symptoms require an urgent call?
Who authorises a treatment hold or restart?
consent_support: Discuss the aim of advanced cancer control, expected benefit and uncertainty, alternatives including not proceeding, bowel and skin effects, serious lung/liver problems, fertility and pregnancy, daily treatment, monitoring and your right to reconsider.

support.title: Diarrhoea and fluids
support.text: Keep the prescribed anti-diarrhoea plan available from the first dose. Report loose stools early and keep drinking if able. Persistent or severe diarrhoea, weakness, inability to drink or much less urine requires urgent advice. The team decides whether to hold treatment and when it is safe to restart.

support.title: Skin, nails and mouth
support.text: Use the agreed skin, nail and mouth-care plan. Report rash, painful nails or mouth sores early. Emollients and sun protection may help; the team decides whether creams, antibiotics or other treatment are needed. Blistering or peeling skin needs urgent assessment.

support.title: Nausea medicines
support.text: Erlotinib has minimal-to-low oral emetic risk. Agree any as-needed anti-sickness medicine with the team. Routine infusion premedication is not required.

support.title: Medicine interactions
support.text: Give pharmacy all medicines and supplements. Strong CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors, grapefruit and medicines for stomach acid can change exposure. Avoid proton pump inhibitor combinations unless the specialist resolves the plan. Necessary antacids require source-specific separation; ask for written timing. Warfarin needs extra blood-clotting checks. Smoking reduces exposure; get cessation support and do not change your cancer dose yourself.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and breastfeeding
support.text: Avoid pregnancy. Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the final dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least 2 weeks after the final dose. Discuss fertility and future pregnancy plans before starting.

chronology_notes.title: Duration
chronology_notes.text: No fixed course cap; continuation depends on benefit and tolerability.

chronology_notes.title: Dose decisions
chronology_notes.text: Dose reductions use 150 → 100 → 50 mg daily. Recovery and restart depend on the specific side effect; only the team may authorise a restart. Do not increase the dose to compensate for smoking or acid-suppressing medicines.
